full_fields.independent_note: The Hindi-labelled field is Latin transliteration. Anas reports the month oath, upper room, Umar’s question, denial of divorce and return after29days. The inserted pre-ila5AH chronology is explanatory apparatus. I initially retain the ila-occasion setting and the actual moon-sighting parenthesis because they locate the exchange and supply the causal premise of is liye; these are source statements, not independently verified dates. All wording and distinct event framing remain literal.

The Urdu fully supplies Anas’s oath/room/Umar dialogue and29-day return. The5AH pre-ila parenthesis is a chronological insertion. The ila occasion and moon-sighting cause appear to function as actual setting and causal narrative, unlike a lexical gloss; I initially retain them. The statement is reported source wording, not an independent chronology claim.

This Hindi slot is Latin. Ikrama reports hearing Abu Hurayrah’s Messenger-attributed seven-hand road decision. I initially retain ki zameen as the actual disputed-property object, with the dispute condition and seven-hand measure intact. No modern unit conversion or wider rule is supplied.

Ikrama/Abu Hurayrah explicitly attributes the road-dispute decision to the Messenger. The parenthetic road-land object appears to supply material scope for the disputed strip; preserve the conditional setting and seven-hand measure, without a modern measurement.

The Hindi-labelled text is Latin. Adi’s hearing from Abdullah ibn Yazid introduces the actual Prophetic prohibition of looting and mutilation. The inline jo Adi bin Sabit ke nana thay is an explanatory chain-identity apposition, not an independently attributed report body; it can remain visible context. The two prohibitions are complete.

The actual report is Abdullah ibn Yazid’s transmission of the Prophet’s two prohibitions. The inline maternal-grandfather relation describes the route identity and should be distinguished as context from that finite prohibition. Do not invent definitions of muslah or a missing event.

This Hindi slot is Latin. Aisha’s curtain with pictures, the Prophet seeing/removing/tearing it, her making two cushions and his sitting on them are all supplied. The when-he-saw parenthesis is actual event sequence. The Aisha-ne-bayan-ki resumption identifies the subsequent first-person maker and is meaningful attribution, not a new Prophetic saying.

The own Urdu supplies the entire curtain/cushions account. Preserve the actual seeing condition and the Aisha reporting resumption before the first-person cushion-making. The two cushions and later sitting are source events; no outside legal inference is added.

The damaged opening omits much of the route and leaves only bin Abdullah before the expedition. Keep that defect rather than importing Urdu’s complete Jabir chain. The Rajab7AH insertion is apparatus; the whatever-rations-remain condition is operative. Wahb’s named first-person question to Jabir is a distinct voice in the same report. I initially retain the fish-body comparison qualifier as the physical basis of the mountain simile. Preserve the literal कहता typo,18nights and camel/rib account.

The full Urdu route names Malik/Wahb/Jabir, unlike the shorter Hindi opening. Jabir’s expedition, remaining-rations order, shortage, fish and ribs are actual. The inserted Rajab7AH date is context. Retain the remaining-rations scope, the Wahb attribution at the intervening question and the physical-body comparison qualifier. Separate that question/reply from the resumed expedition voice without creating another transmitted occurrence.

Latin text occupies the Hindi field. Rafi ibn Khadij explicitly describes praying Asr with the Prophet, slaughtering camel(s), dividing into ten shares and eating cooked meat before sunset. The complete timing and sequence are actual report content, with no compiler tail.

Rafi’s own Urdu supplies the whole Asr/camel/ten-share/cooked-before-sunset sequence. All of it is attributed report content; do not add an inferred duration or normalize the source’s singular/plural wording.

The Hindi-labelled Latin field reports Abdullah ibn Umar’s Prophetic prohibition of taking paired dates without companions’ permission. Dastarkhwan par supplies the shared-meal domain and should remain with the permission limitation; it is not a generic ban on eating dates privately.

Abdullah ibn Umar explicitly attributes this prohibition to the Prophet. Preserve both the permission limitation and the shared-table setting, as well as the actual two-dates-at-once conduct. No additional legal rule is inferred.

Keep Urwah’s framing separate from Aisha’s actual voice.
